quotes.text:
In Ruby 2.4 the `to_time` method for both `DateTime` and `Time` will
preserve the timezone of the receiver when converting to an instance
of `Time`. Since Rails 5.0 will support Ruby 2.2, 2.3 and later we
need to introduce a compatibility layer so that apps that upgrade do
not break. New apps will have a config initializer file that defaults
to match the new Ruby 2.4 behavior going forward.
quotes.author: Andrew White
quotes.title: Add compatibility for Ruby 2.4 `to_time` changes

card.what: This line ensures that `DateTime` objects retain their original timezones when converted to `Time` objects, regardless of the Ruby version being used.
card.why: This line was introduced to maintain compatibility with older Ruby versions (2.2, 2.3) while Rails 5.0 supported newer versions. The Ruby 2.4 release altered the behavior of the `to_time` method for `DateTime` and `Time` objects, so this compatibility layer prevents breaking changes for existing Rails applications. [2]
card.next: Before making any changes, verify that this compatibility layer is still necessary for the intended use cases of the application, considering the current Rails version and the Ruby version being used.

answer: The deprecation had not warned every user, so removing the old to_time behaviour would change return values without warning.
